title: Residential Property Condition Disclosure Report
description: Connecticut General Statutes §20-327b requires sellers of residential real property (1-4 units) to complete and deliver to the buyer a Residential Property Condition Disclosure Report. The report covers 43+ specific property conditions including structural, mechanical, environmental, and known defects. Must be provided before the buyer signs the contract or makes an offer.

required_actions.note: Must be delivered before buyer signs the contract. If not provided, seller may be liable for $300 credit to buyer and full defect liability.

title: Real Estate Agency Disclosure
description: Connecticut General Statutes §20-325f requires licensees to provide written agency disclosure to all parties at the beginning of the first personal meeting to discuss a specific property. Dual agency is permitted with written informed consent of both parties. Designated agency is also recognized.

required_actions.note: Must be presented at first personal meeting to discuss a specific property. Dual agency requires written consent of both buyer and seller.

title: Attorney-Required Closing State
description: Connecticut is an attorney closing state. The Connecticut Unauthorized Practice of Law statutes and bar opinions require that an attorney supervise real estate closings. Attorneys must prepare or review closing documents, examine title, and be present at closing. This applies to both buyer and seller sides.

required_actions.note: Connecticut requires attorney involvement at closing. Both buyer and seller typically have their own attorneys. Title searches must be certified by an attorney.

title: Radon Disclosure and Testing Notice
description: Connecticut General Statutes §20-327b includes radon as a required disclosure item on the Residential Property Condition Disclosure Report. Additionally, CGS §20-327c requires that buyers be informed of the availability and importance of radon testing. Connecticut has elevated radon levels in many areas, particularly in the northwestern highlands.

required_actions.note: Radon disclosure included in the statutory property condition report. Seller must disclose known radon test results and any mitigation systems.

title: Coastal Erosion and Flood Zone Disclosure
description: Connecticut law requires disclosure of property location within coastal area management zones (CGS §22a-94), flood hazard areas, or inland wetlands. Properties in these zones are subject to additional building restrictions and environmental regulations under DEEP jurisdiction.

required_actions.note: Disclose proximity to coastal areas, flood zones, and inland wetlands on the property condition report.
Properties in Coastal Area Management zones require DEEP permits for modifications.
